text: The court is likely to uphold the amendment as applied. Under *Employment Division v. Smith*, a neutral, generally applicable rule does not violate the Free Exercise Clause just because it burdens religiously motivated conduct, and this one denies the benefit to any employee who refuses prescribed care for a reason other than excessive risk, whether that reason is religious or secular. Because the rule has no individualized discretionary exemptions, the strict-scrutiny line of cases (*Sherbert*, *Fulton*) probably does not apply, though the spouse could argue that the exception for excessive risk is a discretionary system. CONFIDENCE: 78
